title: Idempotency and Replayability: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Idempotency and Replayability: Visual Guide

1. Possible Versus Safe | the raw zone from lesson 1 alongside idempotent writes, and how each one fails without the other | raw makes a re-run possible, idempotency makes it safe — replayability needs both

2. Run It Five Times | the July 24 revenue aggregate under append versus partition WRITE_TRUNCATE, as the run count rises | an appended retry doubles the number and nothing errors; a truncate-written partition is byte-identical after one run or five

3. Where Slices Land | Monday's failed load replayed on Wednesday, under event-time versus ingestion-date partitioning | ingestion-date partitioning breaks two days with one replay, because the partition is a function of when the job ran instead of what the data says

4. The Scan Bill | data scanned per year by a daily full refresh versus incremental, as history grows | the full-refresh multiple grows with history while incremental stays flat — but full refresh is self-healing, which is why hybrid is the professional default

5. Watermark Leaks | five source changes tested against WHERE updated_at > watermark | bulk fixes, in-flight commits and hard deletes are invisible to a watermark, so incremental silently rots without a lookback window, soft deletes and periodic reconciliation
